paragraphs: R. Yitzḥak ben Elyashiv. In Sukkah (19, end of side a): Yitzḥak; Tosafot, however, cites there the Jerusalem Talmud's account in chapter Sheloshah She'akhlu: R. Yitzḥak ben Elyashiv. He prayed concerning the wife of R. Mani, the son of R. Yonah, that she become beautiful, Ta'anit, chapter 3 (23b). When he died, seventy tunnels were dug—Rashi explains: [by] thieves. Through his merit there had been no thieves. This is Ein Yaakov's reading; in the Gemara, however, the reading is 'When R. Elyashiv died,' Mo'ed Katan (25b). In Jerusalem Talmud, Avodah Zarah, beginning of chapter 3: when he died, seventy pillars on which the houses rested split [the cited Yerushalmi reads ‘seventy thresholds were uprooted’]. In R. Yoḥanan's time (I did not find this).
